metadata.title: A constructive algorithm for the Lov\'{a}sz Local Lemma on permutations
metadata.authors: David G. Harris and Aravind Srinivasan

nodes.name: Atomic bad-event
nodes.statement: An atomic bad event is a set $B = \{(k_1,x_1,y_1),\dots,(k_r,x_r,y_r)\}$, true iff $\pi_{k_1}(x_1)=y_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \pi_{k_r}(x_r)=y_r$, with no two tuples sharing both an $x$ or both a $y$.

nodes.name: Dependency graph (relation $\sim$)
nodes.statement: Two bad-events satisfy $B \sim B'$ iff there exist $(k,x,y)\in B,(k,x',y')\in B'$ with $x=x'$ or $y=y'$; this defines a negative-dependence graph on $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Witness tree $\hat\tau^T$
nodes.statement: Built from the execution log: starting from the bad-event resampled at time $T$, move backward in time and add each $B$ as a child of the deepest existing $B'$ with $B \sim B'$, otherwise skip $B$.

nodes.name: Witness subdag for $\pi_k$
nodes.statement: A DAG with nodes labeled by pairs $(x,y)$ such that any two nodes overlapping in a coordinate are comparable, and every node has in-degree and out-degree at most two.

nodes.name: Projection $\mathrm{Proj}_k(\tau)$
nodes.statement: For each node $v\in\tau$ labeled by $B$ and each $(k_i,x_i,y_i)\in B$ with $k_i=k$, create a node $v'\approx(x_i,y_i)$; add edges to the deepest predecessor labeled $(k,x,*)$ or $(k,*,y)$ at strictly smaller depth.

nodes.name: Future-subgraph $G_t$
nodes.statement: Defined inductively from $G_0=G$: when bad-event $(k_i,x_i,y_i)$ is encountered at time $t$, remove a source node $(x_i,y_i)$ if present; abort to $\bot$ if a source $(x_i,y'')$ or $(x'',y_i)$ exists with $y''\neq y_i$ or $x''\neq x_i$.

nodes.name: Alternating path
nodes.statement: A simple path in a witness subdag $G$ that alternately proceeds forward and backward along directed edges; for each vertex $v$ the maximal forward and backward paths are uniquely defined since in/out-degrees are $\le 2$.

nodes.name: W-configuration
nodes.statement: An alternating path $(x_0,y_1),(x_1,y_1),(x_1,y_2),\dots,(x_s,y_s),(x_s,y_{s+1})$ ending at a vertex with in-degree at most one and even backward length; the pair $(x_0,y_{s+1})$ is the W-configuration's endpoints.

nodes.name: Active conditions $\mathrm{Active}(G)$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Active}(G) = \{(x,y) \mid (x,y) \text{ are endpoints of a W-configuration of } G\}$; $A_k^t=|\mathrm{Active}(G_{k,t})|$ counts active conditions of permutation $k$ at time $t$.

nodes.name: Latin transversal
nodes.statement: Given an $m\times n$ matrix $A$ with $m\le n$, a Latin transversal is a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ such that no color repeats among the entries $A(i,\pi(i))$, i.e. $A(i,\pi(i))\neq A(i',\pi(i'))$ for $i\neq i'$.

nodes.name: Strong coloring / strong chromatic number
nodes.statement: Given $G$ with vertex partition $V=V_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup V_k$ into blocks of size $b$, a strong coloring assigns each vertex one of $b$ colors so that every block uses all $b$ colors and no edge is monochromatic; the strong chromatic number is the minimum such $b$ that works for any partition.

nodes.name: Independent transversal
nodes.statement: Given $G$ with vertex partition into blocks, an independent transversal selects one vertex from each block such that the selected vertices form an independent set in $G$.

nodes.name: Lopsided LLL for permutations
nodes.statement: If there exists $\mu:\mathcal{B}\to[0,\infty)$ with $\mu(B)\ge P_\Omega(B)\prod_{B'\sim B}(1+\mu(B'))$ for all $B\in\mathcal{B}$, then choosing each $\pi_k$ uniformly at random has positive probability of avoiding all bad-events.
assumptions: Bad-events $\mathcal{B}$ are atomic with negative-dependence graph $\sim$

nodes.name: Change Proposition
nodes.statement: If $\pi_k^{t_0}(X)\neq Y$ and $\pi_k^{t_2}(X)=Y$ for some $t_2>t_0$, then there exists an intermediate time $t_1$ at which a bad-event including $(k,X,*)$ or $(k,*,Y)$ was encountered.
conclusions: $\exists t_1\in[t_0,t_2-1]$: at time $t_1$ a bad-event with $(k,X,*)$ or $(k,*,Y)$ is resampled

nodes.name: Witness Tree Lemma for singleton
nodes.statement: If $\tau$ is a singleton witness tree labeled by $B$, then $P(\tau \text{ appears}) \le P_\Omega(B)$.
assumptions: $\tau$ is a single-node witness tree labeled by $B$

nodes.name: Witness Tree Lemma
nodes.statement: For any witness tree $\tau$ with nodes labeled $B_1,\dots,B_s$, $P(\tau \text{ appears}) \le P_\Omega(B_1)\cdots P_\Omega(B_s)$, with $P_\Omega(B)=\prod_{k=1}^N (n_k-r_k)!/n_k!$ when $B$ contains $r_k$ entries from permutation $k$.
assumptions: $\tau$ is a witness tree with node labels $B_1,\dots,B_s$
Swapping Algorithm starts from a uniformly random initial state

nodes.name: Future-subgraph projection identity
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{Proj}(\hat\tau^T)=G$, then for every $t\le T$ we have $\mathrm{Proj}(\hat\tau^T_{\ge t})=G_t$; in particular, $G_t=\bot$ implies $\mathrm{Proj}(\hat\tau^T)\neq G$.
assumptions: $\hat\tau^T$ is the witness tree at resampling time $T$
$G$ is a fixed witness subdag with future-subgraphs $G_t$
conclusions: If $\mathrm{Proj}(\hat\tau^T)=G$ then $\mathrm{Proj}(\hat\tau^T_{\ge t})=G_t$ for all $t\le T$

nodes.name: Active conditions on $\pi^t$
nodes.statement: If $G=\mathrm{Proj}(\hat\tau^T_{\ge t})$, then for every W-configuration in $G_t$ with endpoints $(x_0,y_{s+1})$ we have $\pi^t(x_0)=y_{s+1}$; in particular, source nodes $(x,y)$ require $\pi^t(x)=y$.
assumptions: $(x_0,y_{s+1})$ are endpoints of a W-configuration in $G_t$

nodes.name: Active-condition change lemma
nodes.statement: Removing source nodes $v_1,\dots,v_r$ from a future-subgraph $G$ yields $H$ admitting an injection $f:Z\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Active}(H)$ with $(x,y)\sim f(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in Z\subseteq\{(x_i,y_i)\}$, and $|\mathrm{Active}(H)|=|\mathrm{Active}(G)|-(r-|Z|)$.
assumptions: $G$ is a future-subgraph with source nodes $v_1\approx(x_1,y_1),\dots,v_r\approx(x_r,y_r)$

nodes.name: Swap probability bound
nodes.statement: Under the constraints $0\le s\le\min(q,r)$, $q+(r-s)\le n$, and the alignment $x_i=x'_i$ or $y_i=y'_i$ for $i=1,\dots,s$, the swap $\pi'=\mathrm{Swap}(\pi;x_1,\dots,x_r)$ satisfies $P(\pi'(x'_1)=y'_1\wedge\dots\wedge\pi'(x'_q)=y'_q)\le \frac{(n-r)!(n-q)!}{n!(n-q-r+s)!}$.
assumptions: $(x'_1,y'_1),\dots,(x'_q,y'_q)$ with all $x'$ distinct, all $y'$ distinct, and $x_i=x'_i$ or $y_i=y'_i$ for $i\le s$

nodes.name: Probability that swap meets active conditions
nodes.statement: If at time $t$ a bad-event $B$ contains $r$ entries from permutation $k$, then $P(\pi_k^{t+1} \text{ satisfies } \mathrm{Active}(G_{k,t+1}))\le P_k(B)\cdot(n_k-A_k^{t+1})!/(n_k-A_k^t)!$.

nodes.name: Constructive LLL for permutations
nodes.statement: If $\mu:\mathcal{B}\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $\mu(B)\ge P_\Omega(B)\prod_{B'\sim B}(1+\mu(B'))$ for all $B$, then the Swapping Algorithm terminates with probability $1$, and the expected number of resamplings of $B$ is at most $\mu(B)$.

nodes.name: Symmetric LLL for permutations
nodes.statement: If every $B\in\mathcal{B}$ has $P_\Omega(B)\le p$ and at most $d$ neighbors in the dependency graph, then $ep(d+1)\le 1$ implies the Swapping Algorithm terminates almost surely with $O(1)$ expected resamplings per bad-event.
assumptions: Every $B$ has at most $d$ neighbors under $\sim$

nodes.name: MT distribution bound for Swapping Algorithm
nodes.statement: If $E\equiv\pi_{k_1}(x_1)=y_1\wedge\dots\wedge\pi_{k_r}(x_r)=y_r$, then the probability that $E$ holds in the output of the Swapping Algorithm is at most $P_\Omega(E)\prod_{B'\sim E}(1+\mu(B'))$.
assumptions: $\mu$ satisfies the LLL criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:constr-lll}
$E$ is a conjunction of permutation-value equalities $\pi_{k_i}(x_i)=y_i$

nodes.name: LFMIS path-length bound
nodes.statement: Let $I\subseteq\mathcal{B}$ be an independent set of true bad-events with $|B|\le M$, and $G=G_{i,j}$ from Step (6). Then with high probability every directed path in $G$ has length $O(M+\log n)$.
assumptions: $I$ an independent set of currently-true bad-events
conclusions: All directed paths in $G_{i,j}$ have length $O(M+\log n)$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Sub-round count bound
nodes.statement: If $|\mathcal{B}|=n^{O(1)}$ and $|B|\le M$ for all $B$, then with high probability $\mathcal{V}_{i,j}=\emptyset$ for some $j=O(M\log^2 n)$.

nodes.name: Witness Tree Lemma in parallel setting
nodes.statement: Ordering resampled bad-events lexicographically by $(i,j,\rho_{i,j})$ yields an execution log under which the Witness Tree Lemma holds: $P(\tau \text{ appears})\le \prod_{B\in\tau}P_\Omega(B)$.
assumptions: Parallel Swapping Algorithm executes with rounds $i$, sub-rounds $j$, ranks $\rho_{i,j}$

nodes.name: Witness-tree height equals round number
nodes.statement: If $B\in I'_{i,j}$ for some $j$ in round $i$ of the Parallel Swapping Algorithm, the witness tree corresponding to its resampling has height exactly $i$.
assumptions: $B$ is resampled at round $i$, sub-round $j$ (i.e. $B\in I'_{i,j}$)
conclusions: The witness tree of $B$'s resampling has height $i$

nodes.name: Round-count bound for Parallel Swapping
nodes.statement: If $\mu(B)\ge(1+\epsilon)P_\Omega(B)\prod_{B'\sim B}(1+\mu(B'))$ for all $B$, then w.h.p. the Parallel Swapping Algorithm terminates in at most $\frac{\log^{O(1)}(n\sum_B \mu(B))}{\epsilon}$ rounds.
conclusions: Parallel Swapping Algorithm terminates in $\frac{\log^{O(1)}(n\sum_B\mu(B))}{\epsilon}$ rounds w.h.p.

nodes.name: Parallel Swapping Algorithm running time
nodes.statement: If $|\mathcal{B}|=n^{O(1)}$, $|B|\le\log^{O(1)} n$, and $\mu(B)\ge(1+\epsilon)P_\Omega(B)\prod_{B'\sim B}(1+\mu(B'))$, then with high probability the Parallel Swapping Algorithm terminates in $\frac{\log^{O(1)}(n\sum_B\mu(B))}{\epsilon}$ time.
conclusions: Parallel Swapping Algorithm runs in $\frac{\log^{O(1)}(n\sum_B\mu(B))}{\epsilon}$ time w.h.p.

nodes.name: Constructive Latin transversal at $(27/256)n$
nodes.statement: If $\Delta\le(27/256)n$ then the matrix $A$ has a Latin transversal, and the Swapping Algorithm finds one in polynomial time.
assumptions: $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix over a color set $C$
Each color appears at most $\Delta\le(27/256)n$ times in $A$
conclusions: Swapping Algorithm constructs such a transversal in polynomial time

nodes.name: Asymptotically optimal $s$-transversals
nodes.statement: If $\Delta\le(s-c\sqrt{s})n$ for sufficiently large constant $c$, then the matrix has a transversal in which no color appears more than $s$ times, constructible in polynomial time.
conclusions: $A$ has an $s$-transversal (no color appears more than $s$ times)
Such a transversal is constructed in polynomial time

nodes.name: Rainbow cycles via Swapping Algorithm
nodes.statement: If $\Delta\le 0.027n$ and $n$ is large enough, then for any $\tau\in S_n$ with no fixed points or 2-cycles there is a Latin transversal $\pi$ conjugate to $\tau$, found by the Swapping Algorithm in polynomial time and the Parallel Swapping Algorithm in $\log^{O(1)} n$ time.
assumptions: $\tau\in S_n$ has no fixed points and no 2-cycles
conclusions: There is a Latin transversal $\pi$ conjugate to $\tau$
Swapping Algorithm finds $\pi$ in polynomial time
Parallel Swapping Algorithm finds $\pi$ in $\log^{O(1)} n$ time

nodes.name: Independent transversal at $b\ge 4\Delta$
nodes.statement: If $b\ge 4\Delta$, then $G$ has an independent transversal, found in expected $O(n\Delta)$ time; an independent transversal containing a fixed vertex $v$ is found in expected $O(n\Delta^2)$ time.
assumptions: $G$ has vertex partition into blocks of size $b$
conclusions: It is found in expected $O(n\Delta)$ time
An independent transversal containing fixed $v$ is found in expected $O(n\Delta^2)$ time

nodes.name: Strong coloring at $b\ge 5\Delta$ via ordinary LLL
nodes.statement: If $b\ge 5\Delta$, then $G$ has a strong coloring constructible in expected $O(n^2\Delta^2)$ time.
assumptions: $G$ has vertex partition into blocks of size $b$
conclusions: It is found in expected $O(n^2\Delta^2)$ time

nodes.name: Strong coloring at $b\ge(256/27)\Delta$ via permutation LLL
nodes.statement: If $b\ge\tfrac{256}{27}\Delta$, then $G$ has a strong coloring found in expected $O(n\Delta)$ time; if $b\ge(\tfrac{256}{27}+\epsilon)\Delta$, an RNC algorithm constructs such a coloring.
assumptions: $G$ has vertex partition into blocks of size $b$
$b\ge \tfrac{256}{27}\Delta$ for the serial version, $b\ge(\tfrac{256}{27}+\epsilon)\Delta$ for the parallel version
conclusions: Swapping Algorithm finds it in expected $O(n\Delta)$ time
Parallel Swapping Algorithm finds it in RNC for $b\ge(\tfrac{256}{27}+\epsilon)\Delta$

nodes.name: Constructive hypergraph packing
nodes.statement: If $(d_1+1)m_2+(d_2+1)m_1<\binom{n}{r}/e$, the Swapping Algorithm finds injections $\phi_i:V(H_i)\to[n]$ with $\phi_1(H_1)$ edge-disjoint from $\phi_2(H_2)$; the parallel version applies in $\log^{O(1)} n/\epsilon$ time when the criterion holds with slack $1-\epsilon$ and $r\le\log^{O(1)} n$.
assumptions: Each edge of $H_i$ intersects $\le d_i$ other edges of $H_i$
conclusions: Swapping Algorithm finds injections $\phi_i:V(H_i)\to[n]$ with $\phi_1(H_1)$ edge-disjoint from $\phi_2(H_2)$
Parallel Swapping Algorithm finds them in $\log^{O(1)} n/\epsilon$ time using $\mathrm{poly}(m_1,m_2,n)$ processors

nodes.name: Swap subroutine domain/range invariance
nodes.statement: For any permutations $\tau,\sigma$, $P(\mathrm{Swap}(\pi;x_1,\dots,x_r)=\sigma)=P(\mathrm{Swap}(\pi\tau;\tau^{-1}x_1,\dots,\tau^{-1}x_r)=\sigma\tau)=P(\mathrm{Swap}(\tau\pi;x_1,\dots,x_r)=\tau\sigma)$.

nodes.name: Swap is order-invariant
nodes.statement: For any $\rho\in S_r$, $P(\mathrm{Swap}(\pi;x_1,\dots,x_r)=\sigma)=P(\mathrm{Swap}(\pi;x_{\rho(1)},\dots,x_{\rho(r)})=\sigma)$.

nodes.name: Swap/Swap2 equivalence
nodes.statement: Define $\mathrm{Swap2}(\pi;y_1,\dots,y_r)=\mathrm{Swap}(\pi^{-1};y_1,\dots,y_r)^{-1}$. If $\pi(x_i)=y_i$ then $P(\mathrm{Swap}(\pi;x_1,\dots,x_r)=\sigma)=P(\mathrm{Swap2}(\pi;y_1,\dots,y_r)=\sigma)$.

nodes.name: Swapping Algorithm
nodes.statement: Generate $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_N$ uniformly at random; while a bad-event $B$ is true, perform $\mathrm{Swap}(\pi_k;x_{i_1},\dots)$ for each permutation $k$ involved in $B$.

nodes.name: Swap subroutine (Fisher-Yates style)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Swap}(\pi;x_1,\dots,x_r)$: for $i=1,\dots,r$ select $x'_i$ uniformly from $[t]\setminus\{x_1,\dots,x_{i-1}\}$ and swap entries $x_i,x'_i$ of $\pi$.
output: Updated permutation $\pi'$ with the entries at $x_1,\dots,x_r$ randomized via Fisher-Yates style swaps

nodes.name: Parallel Swapping Algorithm
nodes.statement: Iterate rounds: in round $i$ form $\mathcal{V}_{i,1}$ of currently-true bad-events, then in each sub-round pick MIS $I_{i,j}$, choose swap-mates, take LFMIS $I'_{i,j}$ under random ordering $\rho_{i,j}$, and apply transpositions in parallel to all $\pi_k$.
input: Polynomially-many atomic bad-events $\mathcal{B}$ with $|B|\le M=\log^{O(1)} n$
output: Permutations $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_N$ in which no $B\in\mathcal{B}$ holds, found in $\log^{O(1)} n$ parallel time w.h.p.

nodes.name: Greedy LFMIS construction
nodes.statement: Orient $G_{i,j}$ along $\rho_{i,j}$; iteratively add all source nodes of $H_s$ to $I'_{i,j}$, remove them with all successors, until $H_s=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Proof of Witness Tree Lemma
nodes.statement: Induction on subtrees: at each step bound the swap probability by $P_k(B)\frac{(n_k-A_k^{t+1})!}{(n_k-A_k^t)!}$ via Proposition~\ref{exchange-prop2}, then telescope through subsequent resamplings; finally absorb the initial $(n_k-A_k^0)!/n_k!$ factor by requiring $\pi^0$ satisfy $\mathrm{Active}(\mathrm{Proj}_k(\tau))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Change Proposition
nodes.statement: Take the earliest $t_1\in[t_0,t_2-1]$ with $\pi_k^{t_1+1}(X)=Y$; the swap that caused it must have moved $x_i\to X$ or $X\to x_i$, exhibiting $(k,X,*)$ or $(k,*,Y)$ in the resampled bad-event.

nodes.name: Proof of Future-subgraph projection identity
nodes.statement: Induction on $t$: split on whether the truncated witness tree $\hat\tau_{\ge t+1}$ contains a $B'\sim B$; both cases match the inductive update rule for $G_t \to G_{t+1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Active conditions on $\pi^t$
nodes.statement: Induction on the W-configuration's base length $s$: base case is a source node, applying Proposition~\ref{change-prop}; inductive step analyzes the bad-event resampling subset and reduces to shorter W-configurations.

nodes.name: Proof of Active-condition change lemma
nodes.statement: Recursively build $Z^i,f^i$, splitting on the forward path of each removed source: cycle/two-forward case, mixed forward/backward case (creates one new W-config), and W-configuration case (destroys one, creates two new W-configs).

nodes.name: Proof of Swap probability bound
nodes.statement: Induction on $s,r$ with cases: (i) $s>0$ and $x_1=x'_1$, (ii) $s>0$ and $y_1=y'_1$ via Swap2 symmetry, (iii) $s=0$ but $(x_i,y_i)\sim(x'_j,y'_j)$ reduces to case $s=1$, (iv) generic $s=0$ via union bound.

nodes.name: Proof of swap-active probability
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma~\ref{active-change-lemma} (relating $A_k^t$ and $A_k^{t+1}$ via injection $f$) with Proposition~\ref{exchange-prop2a} setting $s=|Z|$, $q=A_k^{t+1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Constructive LLL theorem
nodes.statement: By the Witness Tree Lemma, the expected number of resamplings of $B$ is bounded by the sum of $\prod P_\Omega$ over witness trees rooted at $B$, which equals $\mu(B)$ under the LLL criterion (same argument as Moser-Tardos).

nodes.name: Proof of LFMIS path-length bound
nodes.statement: For random $B_1,\dots,B_l\in I$, the probability they form a directed path of length $l=5(M+\log n)$ is $\le\frac{M^{l-1}(|I|-l)!}{(|I|-1)!\,l!}$; union bound over $\le|I|!/(|I|-l)!$ orderings yields $n^{-\Omega(1)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of sub-round count bound
nodes.statement: Using $W(B)\sim U[0,1]$ rank trick and Markov's inequality, show each $B$ stays in $I'$ with probability $\ge 1-1/(2M\ln n)$, giving $\mathbb{E}|\mathcal{V}_{i,j+1}|\le(1-1/(2M\ln n))|\mathcal{V}_{i,j}|$, hence $\mathcal{V}_{i,j}=\emptyset$ at $j=\Omega(M\log^2 n)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Constructive Latin transversal at $(27/256)n$
nodes.statement: Each bad-event $(i,j,i',j')$ has probability $\frac{1}{n(n-1)}$ and four neighbor types, all mutually adjacent. Pegden's criterion reduces to $\alpha\ge\frac{1}{n(n-1)}(1+n(\Delta-1)\alpha)^4$, which has a positive root iff $\Delta\le(27/256)n$.

nodes.name: Proof of asymptotically optimal $s$-transversal
nodes.statement: Use partial resampling with fractional hitting set giving weight $\binom{s}{r}^{-1}$ to each $r$-subset ($r=\lceil\sqrt{s}\rceil$); the LLL criterion $e\binom{s}{r}^{-1}(n-r)!/n!(2rn\binom{\Delta}{r-1}+\binom{\Delta}{r})\le 1$ is satisfied for $\Delta\le(s-O(\sqrt{s}))n$.

nodes.name: Proof of rainbow cycles theorem
nodes.statement: Set $\pi=\sigma^{-1}\tau\sigma$ and apply Swapping Algorithm to $\sigma$. Two bad-event types A/B (with weights $\mu_A=2.83036n^{-4}, \mu_B=1.96163n^{-3}$) and Pegden's criterion yield convergence at $\Delta\le 0.027n$.

nodes.name: Proof of strong coloring at $b\ge 5\Delta$
nodes.statement: Mirroring Aharoni-Berger-Ziv (Theorem 5.3), iteratively complete a partial coloring: pick a missing-color vertex $w$, choose $v_i\in V_i$ with conflict-free swaps via independent transversal (Proposition~\ref{it-prop} requires $b\ge 4\Delta$, swap-feasibility requires $b\ge 5\Delta$).

nodes.name: Proof of strong coloring at $b\ge(256/27)\Delta$
nodes.statement: Each block becomes $S_b$; bad-event $(u,v,c)$ has probability $1/b^2$ and four neighbor types each of size $b\Delta$; Pegden's criterion reduces to $\alpha\ge(1/b^2)(1+b\Delta\alpha)^4$, with positive root for $b\ge(256/27)\Delta$.

nodes.name: Probability of bad-event in $\Omega$
nodes.statement: $P_\Omega(B) = \prod_{k=1}^{N}\frac{(n_k-r_k)!}{n_k!}$ where $B$ contains $r_k$ elements from permutation $k$.

nodes.name: Per-permutation probability $P_k(B)$
nodes.statement: $P_k(B)=\frac{(n_k-r_k)!}{n_k!}$ when bad-event $B$ contains $r_k$ entries from permutation $k$.

nodes.name: $\mu$-form vs. $x$-form of LLL criterion
nodes.statement: The condition $\mu(B)\ge P_\Omega(B)\prod(1+\mu(B'))$ is equivalent to the standard $P_\Omega(B)\le x(B)\prod_{B'\sim B,B'\neq B}(1-x(B'))$ via $\mu(B)=x(B)/(1-x(B))$.

nodes.name: Lopsidependence variant
nodes.statement: Defining $B\sim B'$ to require $x=x',y\neq y'$ or $x\neq x',y=y'$ (so events sharing a triple $(k,x,y)$ are independent) keeps the Witness Tree Lemma valid up to a slight modification of $\mathrm{Proj}_k(\tau)$.

nodes.name: Extension to random injections
nodes.statement: Random injections $f_k:[m_k]\to[n_k]$ are handled by extending to $\pi_k\in S_{n_k}$ with dummy entries $\pi_k(m_k+1),\dots,\pi_k(n_k)$ that participate in no bad-events.

nodes.name: Moser-Tardos algorithm (cited)
nodes.statement: If $\mu(B)\ge\Pr(B)\prod_{B'\sim B}(1+\mu(B'))$ for variable-based events, the Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm terminates with probability one with expected $\mu(B)$ resamplings of $B$.
assumptions: Independent random variables setting (no permutation dependence)

nodes.name: $s$-transversal existence
nodes.statement: Given an $m\times n$ matrix $A$ with each value appearing at most $\Delta$ times, find the maximum $\Delta=L(s;m,n)$ guaranteeing an $s$-transversal: a transversal in which no value appears more than $s$ times.

nodes.name: Latin transversal construction
nodes.statement: Given an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ with $\Delta\le(27/256)n$, construct in polynomial time a Latin transversal of $A$.

nodes.name: Strong coloring construction
nodes.statement: Given $G$ with vertex partition into blocks of size $b$ and max-degree $\Delta$, construct a strong coloring (every block uses all $b$ colors and no edge is monochromatic).

nodes.name: Edge-disjoint hypergraph packing
nodes.statement: Given $r$-uniform hypergraphs $H_1,H_2$ and integer $n$, find injections $\phi_i:V(H_i)\to[n]$ such that $\phi_1(H_1)$ and $\phi_2(H_2)$ are edge-disjoint.

nodes.name: Inductive bound on subtree probability
nodes.statement: Show by induction on $\tau'$ that $P(\hat\tau^T=\tau' \text{ for some }T\ge0)\le\prod_{B\in\tau'}P_\Omega(B)\prod_k\frac{n_k!}{(n_k-|\mathrm{Active}(\mathrm{Proj}_k(\tau'))|)!}$, vacuous for $\tau'=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Bound first resampling via Proposition 5.2
nodes.statement: Conditioning on $v\in\tau'$ being the first resampled node at time $t$: $P(\pi^{t+1}\text{ satisfies active conditions})\le\prod_k P_k(B)\frac{(n_k-A_k^{t+1})!}{(n_k-A_k^t)!}$ by Proposition~\ref{exchange-prop2}.

nodes.name: Multiply by inductive subtree bound
nodes.statement: Multiply the swap-success bound by the inductive bound on $\tau'-v$ to obtain $\prod_{B\in\tau'}P_\Omega(B)\prod_k n_k!/(n_k-A_k^t)!$, completing the induction.

nodes.name: Discharge initial-state factor
nodes.statement: Multiply by the probability $(n_k-A_k^0)!/n_k!$ that the initial $\pi^0_k$ satisfies $\mathrm{Active}(\mathrm{Proj}_k(\tau))$; the resulting product telescopes to $\prod_{B\in\tau}P_\Omega(B)$.

nodes.name: Case $s>0$ and $x_1=x'_1$
nodes.statement: First swap forces $x_1\leftrightarrow\pi^{-1}(y'_1)$ with probability $1/n$; the residual problem on $\pi(x_1\,x'')$ has parameters $(n-1,r-1,s-1,q-1)$ and yields $\frac{1}{n}g(n-1,r-1,s-1,q-1)=g(n,r,s,q)$.

nodes.name: Case $s>0$ and $y_1=y'_1$ via Swap2
nodes.statement: Apply Swap/Swap2 equivalence (Proposition~\ref{exchange-sym-prop}) to swap roles of $x_1,y_1$, reducing to the previous case.

nodes.name: Case $s=0$ with overlap
nodes.statement: If some $(x_i,y_i)\sim(x'_j,y'_j)$, reorder via Proposition~\ref{swap-invariant-prop2} to $(x_1,y_1)\sim(x'_1,y'_1)$ and reduce to the $s=1$ case, giving $g(n,r,1,q)\le g(n,r,0,q)$.

nodes.name: Case $s=0$ generic via union bound
nodes.statement: Bound $P(\pi'(x'_j)=y'_j\,\forall j)\le \sum_{y''_1,\dots,y''_r}P(\pi'(x_i)=y''_i\,\forall i)$; each summand is $\le g(n,r,r,q)$ by induction, with $(n-q)!/(n-q-r)!$ summands, giving $g(n,r,0,q)$.

nodes.name: Case 1: cycle / both forward
nodes.statement: Forward path is a cycle or has forward edges on both sides: no W-configurations created or destroyed, so $|\mathrm{Active}(H_i)|=|\mathrm{Active}(H_{i-1})|-1$ and $Z^i=Z^{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Case 2: mixed forward/backward
nodes.statement: Forward path has one forward and one backward end: removal creates one new W-configuration with endpoint $(x_i,Y_{s+1})$; update $Z^i=Z^{i-1}\cup\{(x_i,y_i)\}$ with $f^i(x_i,y_i)=(x_i,Y_{s+1})$, $|\mathrm{Active}|$ unchanged.

nodes.name: Case 3: W-configuration
nodes.statement: Forward path is itself a W-configuration: removal destroys one W-configuration and creates two new ones with endpoints $(X_0,Y_j),(X_j,Y_{s+1})$; reroute $f^{i-1}$ accordingly to keep $|\mathrm{Active}|$ unchanged.

nodes.name: Base case: source node
nodes.statement: For source $(x,y)$, suppose $\pi^t(x)\neq y$; by Proposition~\ref{change-prop} an earlier bad-event $(x,*),(*,y)$ would create a source node conflicting with $(x,y)$.

nodes.name: Inductive step on W-configuration length
nodes.statement: Resampling future bad-event $B$ removes some source nodes and creates shorter W-configurations whose endpoints by IH must equal corresponding $\pi^{t'+1}$ values; tracking the swap sequence forces $\pi^t(x_0)=y_{s+1}$.

nodes.name: Path-probability estimate
nodes.statement: For random $B_1,\dots,B_l\in I$ without replacement, $\rho(B_1)<\dots<\rho(B_l)$ has probability $1/l!$, and each consecutive overlap has probability $\le M/(|I|-s)$, yielding $\frac{M^{l-1}(|I|-l)!}{(|I|-1)!l!}$.

nodes.name: Union bound over orderings
nodes.statement: Multiplying by $|I|!/(|I|-l)!\le n^l$ orderings yields $\le n M^{l-1}/(l/e)^l = n^{-\Omega(1)}$ for $l=5(M+\log n)$.

nodes.name: Survival probability for $B$ in LFMIS
nodes.statement: Using $W(B)=w$ and integrating the conditional bound $\mathbb{E}[\#\text{conflicts}]\le wM\ln n$ via Markov, $P(B\in I')\ge 1-1/(2M\ln n)$.

nodes.name: Geometric decay of $\mathcal{V}_{i,j}$
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}|\mathcal{V}_{i,j+1}|\le(1-1/(2M\ln n))|\mathcal{V}_{i,j}|$, so $|\mathcal{V}_{i,j}|\le n^{-\Omega(1)}$ at $j=\Omega(M\log^2 n)$, hence empty w.h.p.

nodes.name: Bad-event probability and neighbors
nodes.statement: Each bad-event $(i,j,i',j')$ has probability $1/(n(n-1))$; each of four neighbor types contributes $n(\Delta-1)$ candidates and neighbors of one type are mutually adjacent.

nodes.name: Pegden's criterion application
nodes.statement: Pegden's criterion gives sufficient condition $\alpha\ge \frac{1}{n(n-1)}(1+n(\Delta-1)\alpha)^4$, which by routine algebra has a positive real root iff $\Delta\le(27/256)n$.

nodes.name: Setup: A-events and B-events with weights
nodes.statement: Set $\pi=\sigma^{-1}\tau\sigma$, classify bad-events as type A (color repeats in distinct rows/columns) and B (column-of-one equals row-of-other), assigning weights $\mu_A=2.83036n^{-4}$, $\mu_B=1.96163n^{-3}$.

nodes.name: Bounds for $t,s,b$
nodes.statement: Derive $t\le 2n^3\Delta\mu_A$ (sum of weights involving fixed $\sigma(x)$), $s\le n^3\Delta\mu_A$ (events led by fixed $i$), $b\le n^2(\Delta/2)\mu_B$ (B-events alone).

nodes.name: Independent-set sums and Pegden criteria
nodes.statement: Independent-set sums of neighbors give $\mu_A\ge\frac{(n-4)!}{n!}(1+t)^4(1+b+sb+s+s^2+s+s)^2$ and $\mu_B\ge\frac{(n-3)!}{n!}(1+t)^3(1+b+sb+sb+s+s^2+s^2+s+s^2+s)$.

nodes.name: Solving for $\Delta\le 0.027n$
nodes.statement: Symbolic algebra shows the system has solutions with the chosen $\mu_A,\mu_B$ when $\Delta\le 0.027n$ and $n$ is large; Swapping/Parallel-Swapping then return $\sigma$ and hence $\pi=\sigma^{-1}\tau\sigma$.

nodes.name: Initialize permutations
nodes.statement: Generate $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_N$ uniformly at random and independently.

nodes.name: Main resampling loop
nodes.statement: While there is some true bad-event $B\in\mathcal{B}$, pick one arbitrarily and proceed to resampling.

nodes.name: Resample bad-event via Swap
nodes.statement: For each permutation $k$ involved in $B$, simultaneously $\mathrm{Swap}(\pi_k;x_{i_1},\dots,x_{i_l})$ over all $(k,x_{i_j},y_{i_j})\in B$.

nodes.name: Iterate selection of $x'_i$
nodes.statement: For $i=1,\dots,r$: select $x'_i$ uniformly from $[t]\setminus\{x_1,\dots,x_{i-1}\}$.

nodes.name: Apply transposition
nodes.statement: Swap entries $x_i$ and $x'_i$ of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Parallel initialization
nodes.statement: Generate $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_N$ uniformly at random in parallel.

nodes.name: Round loop on $\mathcal{V}_{i,1}$
nodes.statement: Round $i=1,2,\dots$: set $\mathcal{V}_{i,1}$ to the bad-events true at the start of round $i$; iterate sub-rounds.

nodes.name: Sub-round MIS
nodes.statement: For sub-round $j=1,2,\dots$ while $\mathcal{V}_{i,j}\neq\emptyset$: compute MIS $I_{i,j}\subseteq\mathcal{V}_{i,j}$ using a parallel MIS algorithm.

nodes.name: Sample swap-mates without applying
nodes.statement: For each $B\in I_{i,j}$, pre-select swap-mates $z_l$ for each $(k_l,x_l,y_l)\in B$ but do not perform the swaps yet.

nodes.name: Build conflict graph and LFMIS
nodes.statement: Pick random ordering $\rho_{i,j}$, build conflict graph $G_{i,j}$ (edge $B\to B'$ if a swap-mate of $B$ is a swap-source of $B'$ and $\rho_{i,j}(B)<\rho_{i,j}(B')$), select LFMIS $I'_{i,j}$ via the greedy algorithm.

nodes.name: Apply ordered transpositions
nodes.statement: For each $\pi_k$, compose all transpositions $(x\;z)$ from $I'_{i,j}$ in $\rho_{i,j}$-order: $\pi'_k=\pi_k(x_l\,z_l)\cdots(x_1\,z_1)$.

nodes.name: Update $\mathcal{V}_{i,j+1}$
nodes.statement: Form $\mathcal{V}_{i,j+1}$ by removing from $\mathcal{V}_{i,j}$ all bad-events no longer true under the new permutations or connected via $\sim$ to any element of $I'_{i,j}$.

nodes.name: Orient edges along $\rho_{i,j}$
nodes.statement: Let $H_1$ be $G_{i,j}$ with all edges oriented in the direction of $\rho_{i,j}$.

nodes.name: Source extraction loop
nodes.statement: For $s=1,2,\dots$ while $H_s\neq\emptyset$: find all source nodes of $H_s$, add to $I'_{i,j}$, then form $H_{s+1}$ by removing sources and their successors.

nodes.name: Return LFMIS
nodes.statement: Return $I'_{i,j}$, the lexicographically-first MIS of $G_{i,j}$ under $\rho_{i,j}$.
